title: Summer
hookLine: holidays and rest, and Mass wherever you are
tomorrow: who do you thank for a plate of food?

lines: COME APART, AND REST A LITTLE.
cards: Out-of-office on, sunscreen in the bag, a rental with a shower nobody can figure out. Summer is when the routine breaks, and Sunday Mass is easy to lose in the shuffle.

Jesus once told his worn-out disciples, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Rest is his idea. The question is whether God gets left at home with the houseplants.

teach.b: Mark sets the scene: so many people were coming and going that the disciples had no time even to eat. Jesus doesn't scold them for being tired. He takes them away in a boat.
Rest is part of the life, not a break from it.

teach.h: EVEN THERE SHALL THY HAND LEAD ME.
teach.b: And a psalm answers the other half, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "If I take my wings early in the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea: Even there also shall thy hand lead me." No beach is out of range.
The Church asks Catholics to keep Sunday at Mass, and church law says that's met at Mass in any Catholic rite, anywhere.
So on vacation you look up the nearest parish, and you might hear the Mass in a language you don't speak. Here's the part to tell a friend tonight: you'll still know where you are.
The sign of the cross, the readings, the Holy, holy, the bread lifted up, the Our Father, the sign of peace. In the Roman Rite the shape is the same, and your body knows it.
Strangers sing a melody you've never heard, and you stand when they stand.
The catechism says the word catholic means universal.
One family, many languages, one table.

how: Catholics on vacation look up a nearby parish's Mass times and keep Sunday wherever they are; church law says the Sunday obligation is met at Mass celebrated in any Catholic rite.

o: plan the hour: Mass first or last, the beach around it.

games.why: Jesus calls the tired to rest, and the Church keeps Sunday at Mass anywhere. with a plan, both fit in one day.

practice: Stand up and take a slow walk, even just across the room and back, as if you were somewhere new on vacation.

Notice what your feet already know how to do without thinking, the way your body knows the shape of the Mass in any language. As you walk, let the psalm go with you: even there also shall thy hand lead me.

wordCard.voice: Summer. The season of rest, with God along for the trip and Sunday Mass found wherever you are.

orig.note: Greek: universal, the word behind catholic.

carryVoice: Keep this: God on holiday too, and no beach out of range of that hand. See you tomorrow.
